t: Section 633(c) of title 28, United States Code, is amended by striking out the final sentence.

fable.w: This is a purely technical amendment that strikes a sentence from an existing provision of title 28. Nothing in the text creates consultation, a hearing, a comment period, rulemaking, an advisory body, or a right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. There is no tempting contrary reading, since the section names no outside party and no participatory process.
fable.s: Section 633(c) of title 28, United States Code, is amended by striking out the final sentence.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely procedural amendment instruction that removes text from another statute. It does not itself establish any process for public participation, consultation, or coordination with outside entities. The text provided contains no actors, decisions, or mechanisms involving non-federal parties.
qwen_block.s: Section 633(c) of title 28, United States Code, is amended by striking out the final sentence.

opus.w: This is a purely technical amendment that deletes a sentence from 28 U.S.C. 633(c). It does not create or require any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. Any guess about what the deleted sentence said would go beyond the text, and the judicial bodies involved in section 633 are inside the federal government anyway.
opus.s: Section 633(c) of title 28, United States Code, is amended by striking out the final sentence.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Section 633 of title 28 sets out how the number, locations and salaries of U.S. magistrates are determined. Those decisions can involve input from district courts, so someone might assume the amendment touches a consultation process. That reading fails. The text only deletes a sentence. It does not name any outside party, any consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue. With nothing on the face of the section showing a non-federal party taking part in a federal decision, the definition is not met.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a legislative amendment instruction that removes text from an existing statute. It does not establish any new process for consultation, public comment, or coordination with outside parties. The mere reference to a section of the U.S. Code does not imply participation; the action described is purely editorial/legislative.
qwen_chat.s: Section 633(c) of title 28, United States Code, is amended by striking out the final sentence.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might assume that because the text references "Section 633(c) of title 28," which likely deals with judicial conduct or complaints (often involving public participation), the amendment itself involves participation. However, the text provided is merely an instruction to delete a sentence. It does not describe any process of consultation, hearing, or coordination with outside parties. It is a legislative directive to modify existing law, not a procedural requirement for participation in a decision.
